completion_data.completion_summary: Redesigned the /email staleness detector from an unreachable on-disk-files-vs-deduped-messages equality gate to a reachable file-vs-file comparison with bounded tolerance and a reindex-ran marker, propagated across staleness-detection.md, cross-repo census.nix/mbsync.nix (written, not built), wrapper-contracts.md, skill-email-cleanup SKILL.md, and lower-stakes docs, verified live to reach [ok] for both Gmail and Logos; two independent anomalies (22 unindexed Logos files, --account positional-arg bug) recommended as follow-up tasks.

memory_candidates.content: When a freshness/staleness gate compares an on-disk file count against a notmuch count, use notmuch --output=files post-filtered by literal path prefix (e.g. `notmuch search --output=files 'path:X/cur or path:X/new' | grep -cE '/X/(cur|new)/'`), never `notmuch count folder:X` (deduped Message-ID count, wrong unit) nor a raw `notmuch count --output=files folder:X` (notmuch's --output=files returns ALL known files for a matching message across every folder/account, not just the queried folder — verified: folder:Gmail --output=files=238 vs 128 real files). Pair a file-vs-file comparison with a bounded tolerance (e.g. Δ=|on-disk-indexed|, T=max(5,ceil(0.10*on-disk))) rather than strict equality, since a small irreducible residual (duplicate-free but still-unindexed files) can make strict equality permanently unreachable for some accounts.

For a non-interactive implementation agent, task-system follow-up creation (/task, /spawn) requiring an interactive AskUserQuestion confirmation gate should be handled by recording concrete, actionable recommendations (with full diagnostic context / dead-ends ruled out) in the implementation summary rather than attempting to hand-roll state.json/TODO.md task entries directly. This preserves both scope discipline (no drive-by fix of the out-of-scope item) and correctness of the task-creation machinery (numbering, interactive confirmation) that only the proper /task or /spawn flow provides.
